text: Lamplighter. A bounded A.I. revenue-recovery agent for Razorpay merchants, rendered as a cozy town. Built for the Razorpay A.I. Buildathon, track three, by Nipun Arora.

Saanjh and Co. is a small tea and candle studio in Jaipur. Every week, money slips away in undramatic ways. A U.P.I. request times out. A card hits its daily limit. A bank is down for ten minutes. An AutoPay mandate gets paused. A cafe's wholesale invoice drifts past due. Each one is recoverable. Chasing them by hand is slow, and a dumb cron annoys customers and breaks rules.
In Lamplighter, every customer is a house, and every payment at risk is a dark lantern. The agent is a lamplighter who walks the streets and relights them, inside the rules.

Press Light the lamps. Every case is diagnosed first. Razorpay's structured error handles the easy ones. A local Qwen model, running on this laptop, reads raw bank strings like U thirty, debit has been failed, and classifies them. Then the policy engine enumerates every possible action and runs every rule. The model only chooses among what is already allowed, and every outreach creates a real Razorpay test-mode order.

Click a house. Here is the Razorpay error, the diagnosis with its confidence and source, and every candidate action with the rules it passed or failed. A silent retry is blocked when the issuer says do not retry. A voice call is blocked when the amount is too small for a call. The message goes out in the customer's language, Hinglish or English, validated for the exact amount, the merchant name and an opt-out line, and it links to a checkout page backed by a real order.

This is the loop closing for real. The customer opens the pay page, pays through Razorpay Checkout, the server verifies the H.M.A.C. signature, captures the payment, and the lantern lights. A payment that lands without the browser callback is caught by polling the order.

At nine at night, the lamplighter stops. Quiet hours are part of the world, not a footnote. Deferred actions show up in the journal for nine a.m. A customer who replies STOP ends contact immediately, including any retry already scheduled. Three knocks maximum, no repeats, D.N.D. respected, and every extra knock costs goodwill in the expected-value math.

The numbers. On one hundred and twenty cases over a simulated fortnight, Lamplighter recovered three lakh forty-one thousand rupees of ten point seven lakh at risk, against one lakh thirty-six thousand for a naive retry cron on the same customers. Fifty-nine cases against nineteen. Half the touches. Eleven complaints against fifty-five. Zero policy violations against three hundred and fifty-eight. Diagnosis accuracy went from seventy-two percent with rules alone to one hundred percent with the local model. Across ten different seeded worlds, the agent wins ten of ten on money and on complaints, and the confidence interval excludes zero. The customers are simulated, with hidden state the agent never reads, and the report says so.

Failure is exercised, not promised. Chaos injection makes Razorpay and the model fail on demand. Retries with backoff. A circuit breaker the engine waits out. Template fallbacks when the model's draft breaks a rule. A hash-chained audit log anyone can verify. Twenty-five tests, and continuous integration that runs a whole batch with no external services at all.
Escalations go to humans with a packet of what was tried. That is Lamplighter. Bounded. Explainable. Measured. Thank you.
